meal.name: Sunday Roast — Complete Menu
meal.workflow_md:
*Serves 3 (2 carb-moderate adults + teen) · 1.18 kg compact tied MB3+ rib eye, 12 cm dia · Service 7:05pm, Sun 12 Jul · Register: classic, generous, restrained* ## Menu - Rib eye roast (reverse sear) - Duck-fat roast potatoes (split-roast) - Honey-glazed carrots (light honey) - Green beans, butter + lemon zest - Horseradish cream - Red wine jus (staged) ## Critical Path Potato pre-roast → beef low roast → beef rest (potato recrisp overlaps) → potato out → oven to max → beef blast → carve. Single Bosch oven; every oven transition is gated by the oven reaching temperature, not by elapsed time — the clock is the planning path, not a guarantee. Horseradish is made ahead and never gates service. **Failure prioritization:** Protect beef core temp and the final potato crisp. Governing rule — the beef's 40-min rest ceiling outranks potato recrisp duration and nominal service time. If a transition compresses the recrisp, pull potatoes at achieved crust; the beef blast does not wait. ## Oven Sequencing (single Bosch — state-gated) - 450°F / 230°C — potato pre-roast. Potatoes enter only once the oven actually reads 450°F. - 250°F / 121°C — beef low roast. After pre-roast, drop the setting and briefly vent the door (450→250 with door shut is slow); beef enters only once near 250°F. - ≥425–450°F / 220–230°C — potato recrisp. Begins once genuinely recovered. - Max / 500°F — beef blast. Begins once the oven reaches actual max. ## Parallel vs. Sequential - Parallel: carrots (induction 1), beans blanch-then-hold (induction 2), jus on outdoor gas burner (keeps both induction burners free). Horseradish done ahead. - Sequential (oven-bound): potato pre-roast → beef low → potato recrisp → beef blast. One owner at a time. ## T-Minus Timeline *Planning path, 7:05pm service. Beef pull temp is the master trigger; oven transitions are temperature-gated. The clock is the on-time estimate — the trigger band below governs deviation.*
TimeAction
Sat eveningCut + re-tie roast done, 1.18 kg. Dry-brine 12 g Diamond Crystal (1%), uncovered on rack, fridge, ~24 hr
3:45 pmBeef out of fridge (~70 min before roasting — takes surface chill off; do not wait for center to reach room temp). Make horseradish if not done
3:55 pmOven → 450°F. Parboil potatoes (baking soda), drain, rough, dry
~4:05 pmOnce oven reads 450°F: potatoes pre-roast, aim to finish ~4:40–4:45 — pale gold, set, not yet deeply crisp
~4:40–4:45 pmPotatoes out → hold uncovered, single layer, wire rack, room temp. Drop oven to 250°F, vent door briefly. (If beef start shifts later, delay the pre-roast rather than hold potatoes past 2 hr.)
4:45 pmJus stage 1: brown 1 sliced shallot (+ optional trimmings) in a little oil on outdoor gas; deglaze with wine, reduce by half; add stock, brief simmer, then off heat, covered
4:50 pmBeef: pat bone-dry, oil, pepper, insert probe (alarm 116°F)
~4:55 pmOnce oven near 250°F: beef in (~75–80 min, probe-governed)
6:05 pmJus stage 2: return to gas, finish stock reduction to a light nappe. Begin watching probe
6:15 pmBeef pulls at 119–120°F. Onto rack, rest uncovered. Oven → back up to 450°F. Fold low-roast drippings into jus
~6:28–6:30 pmOnce oven ≥425–450°F: potatoes back in, recrisp ~15–20 min — pull when deeply golden and audibly crisp, turning once. Watch the garlic/thyme
6:35 pmCarrots on induction 1; bean water to boil on induction 2
~6:40–6:43 pmJus stage 3: add drippings, strain, mount 20 g cold butter, hold warm on lowest gas. Blanch beans 4 min, shock, drain, hold
~6:48 pmPotatoes out at achieved crisp → hold on rack, room temp. Oven → max
~6:54 pmOnce oven at max: beef in, blast 5–8 min, crust-color-governed
6:57 pmToss beans butter + zest, low induction. Plate carrots
~7:00–7:02 pmBeef out when crust set. Thermapen-verify ~127–133°F. Add final-blast drippings to jus
7:05 pmHandling done — carve against grain. Plate; jus + horseradish to table
### Trigger band (governs deviation) - Pull 6:14–6:20: normal path, hold ~7:05 service. - Pull 6:10–6:13: advance potato exit, oven-to-max, and blast by the matching minutes; potatoes accept a shorter recrisp. - Pull before 6:10: advance the whole final sequence, accept earlier service. Don't extend the rest to protect 7:05. - Pull after 6:20: shift service later; carrots and beans wait, beef doesn't. *Verification: Beef rest 6:15→~6:54 = ~39 min, under 40 ✓. Potato recrisp sensory-governed ~15–20 min ✓. Jus staged with hold, not continuously reduced ✓. Blast + handling → 7:05 carve ✓. Transitions state-gated, none assumed instantaneous ✓.* ## Holding Chain
ComponentHold StrategyMax HoldDrift RiskCorrective
BeefRack, uncovered, room temp40 minOver-rest cools coreBlast reheats surface; Thermapen-verify post-blast
Potatoes (pre-roast)Wire rack, room temp, single layer~2 hrSurface dries (harmless)Recrisp restores; never stack/cover
Potatoes (final)Wire rack, room temp, single layer~10 minCrust softensUncovered, never cover
CarrotsCovered pan, residual heat15 minGlaze tightensLoosen with splash of water off-heat
Green beansDrained, dry, room temp15 minLose glossButter + zest toss at 6:57
JusWarm, lowest gas30 minOver-reducesLoosen with stock; re-strain
HorseradishFridge, coveredDaysNoneServe cold
## Plating Window Beef out of blast ~7:00–7:02 when crust set; 2–3 min handling/transfer (not a formal rest). 7:05 carve against the grain, ~1 cm. Plate carrots at 6:57, beans tossed in butter + zest at 6:57; jus + horseradish to table. ## Meal Balance Audit Richness: beef + duck fat + butter jus — high, relieved by green beans (fresh-firm reset), horseradish (cold sharp cut), and lemon zest aroma. Acid: horseradish (cultured cream + vinegar) and wine reduction across the savoury plate; lemon juice as adjustment. Distinct roles throughout — no redundancy. Sweet: carrots (light honey), single and isolated. Texture: crisp potato + beef crust vs. tender beef + soft carrots, green beans as firm anchor. No monotony, no accumulation gap.
meal.shared_prep_md:
- **Lemon:** zest 1 → beans; juice → reserve for adjustments (horseradish, carrots, jus).
- **Butter (cold, cubed):** 60 g total — 20 g → jus mount, 20 g → carrots, 20 g → beans.
- **Diamond Crystal salt:** 12 g → beef brine (Sat); remainder to season potatoes/carrots/beans to taste.
- **Jus base:** 1 sliced shallot browned in a little oil (default); beef trimmings optional additive.

*Sourcing: Ask the butcher for trimmings when collecting the roast — free jus-base boost. Horseradish cream: taste before adding lemon or salt — prepared horseradish carries its own vinegar and salt.*

dishes.name: Rib Eye Roast (Reverse Sear)
dishes.source: Recovered from rib-eye-roast-sunday.docx, generated for service Sun 12 Jul 2026 (no generation date stated in doc)
dishes.summary: MB3+ boneless rib eye dry-brined 24 hr, roasted at 250°F to a probe-governed 119–120°F pull, rested under 40 min, then blasted in a max oven for a single deep crust and an even medium-rare (~127–133°F).
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview MB3+ boneless rib eye roasted low to an even medium-rare, then blasted hot for a single deep crust. Uniform rosy interior wall-to-wall, deep-browned exterior, beef unmasked. Crust built once, at the end. ## Yield & Timing *Yield: serves 3 with leftovers · Total ~3.5 hr incl. temper · Active ~25 min · Oven 250°F → max* ## Flavor Architecture
ElementDefinition
BaseRendered beef fat + oil film for sear conduction
Primary driverThe beef — MB3+ marbling; no competing element
AcidNone in the roast — externalized to horseradish + jus (meal-level)
Aromatic/finishBlack pepper; thyme background
*Meal-level carve-out: acid provided by horseradish and jus, not the roast.* ## Texture Two distinct — yielding interior vs. crisp-browned crust. The final blast is the entire crust mechanism. ## Prep Phase 1. Sat: cut + re-tie done, 1.18 kg. Salt all surfaces evenly (12 g). Rack, uncovered, fridge, ~24 hr — dries surface, seasons deep. 1% is moderate and sufficient; the meat needs no finishing salt by default — taste a slice first. 2. 3:45pm Sun: out of fridge, ~70 min before roasting — takes the surface chill off; do not wait for the center to reach room temp. Pat bone-dry before roasting. 3. 4:50pm: rub with 1 tbsp oil, crack pepper all over. No additional salt. ## Active Cooking 1. Oven 250°F / 121°C. Leave-in probe (ThermoWorks) into thickest center, alarm 116°F. 2. Roast to pull — probe-governed (~75–80 min; 12 cm diameter drives this, not weight). Pull at 119–120°F / 48–49°C. 3. Rest uncovered on rack ~39 min (40 min ceiling). Oven → 450°F for potato recrisp, then → max in the final minutes. 4. Final blast: into max oven (500°F / 260°C), 5–8 min, crust-color-governed. A 1.18 kg roast climbs fast — watch it. 5. Verify: Thermapen the center post-blast. Expect ~127–133°F / 53–56°C — verify, don't assume a fixed rise. The probe number is the truth. ## Holding & Assembly Off the blast, 2–3 min handling/transfer (not a formal rest — the pre-blast rest already redistributed juices). Carve against the grain, ~1 cm. Jus + horseradish to table. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & CueRecovery
CriticalOvershoot core — pulled too high or blasted too long. Cue: Thermapen >133°F post-blast → past medium-rare, grey bandUnrecoverable. Prevention: pull 119–120°F, blast by crust color not clock, verify with Thermapen
MajorWeak crust — surface not dry, or oven didn't recover to max. Cue: pale exterior after blastExtend blast 1–2 min watching center; if core near limit, accept lighter crust (serviceable)
MinorOff-center probe → uneven read. Cue: one end more doneCosmetic — serve to preference
## Adjustment Notes The meat is moderately salted from the brine — taste a slice before any finishing salt; jus and horseradish also carry salt. If flat, a few flakes at the plate, not the board. ## Scaling Notes Diameter governs low-roast time more than weight — 12 cm compact runs ~75–80 min. A long/narrow roast of the same weight runs faster with more crust. Below 1 kg, drop blast to 4–5 min.

dishes.source: Recovered from rib-eye-roast-sunday.docx, generated for service Sun 12 Jul 2026 (no generation date stated in doc)
dishes.summary: Peeled Yukon/Maris potatoes parboiled with baking soda, roughed up, pre-roasted in shimmering duck fat at 450°F to set, held on a rack, then recrisped ~15–20 min during the beef rest for a craggy shattering crust.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview Parboiled potatoes pre-roasted to set, held, then recrisped during the beef rest — a shattering craggy crust and fluffy interior in duck fat. Baking soda in the parboil raises surface pH so the exterior crisps aggressively. The split solves the single-oven bottleneck. ## Yield & Timing *Yield: serves 3 · Total ~55 min across two phases · Active ~15 min · Oven 450°F / 230°C* ## Flavor Architecture
ElementDefinition
BaseDuck fat (roasting medium + flavor)
Primary driverPotato + duck fat richness
AcidNone — externalized to meal
Aromatic/finishGarlic + thyme in the fat; salt at finish
*Single-stage acceptable: no acid by design; richness component, acid externalized.* ## Texture Two distinct — craggy crisp shell vs. fluffy interior, via baking-soda parboil + roughing-up. ## Prep Phase 1. Peel (skin blocks crust and steams under the fat). Even ~4 cm chunks. 2. Parboil in salted water + ¼ tsp baking soda, ~8 min from boil, until edges just soften. 3. Drain thoroughly, dry in the hot pan 30 sec, then shake hard in the colander to rough the surfaces — roughed edges become the crust. ## Active Cooking 1. Pre-roast: heat duck fat in the tray in the 450°F oven ~5 min until shimmering. Add potatoes (dry — spatter risk), turn to coat, add garlic/thyme if using. Roast to pale gold and structurally set, ~25–30 min. Remove; hold uncovered, single layer, wire rack, room temp. 2. Recrisp: once the oven has recovered to ≥425–450°F during the beef rest, return potatoes ~15–20 min, turning once, until deeply golden and audibly crisp. Salt out of the oven. ## Holding & Assembly Pre-roasted potatoes hold up to ~2 hr on the rack, room temp. Final crisped potatoes hold ~10 min. Never stack or cover at any stage — trapped steam softens the crust instantly. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & CueRecovery
MajorSoft, greasy — fat not hot at entry, or crowded tray. Cue: pale, oil-slickedSpread out, raise to 475°F, extend. Prevention: fat shimmering before entry; single layer
MajorOver-browned crags / scorched garlic on recrisp — too long at true 450°F. Cue: dark bitter edges, acrid garlicRecoverable for potatoes (pull immediately); discard scorched aromatics. Prevention: sensory-govern the recrisp, pull when golden not dark
MinorOver-roughed → mushy exterior. Cue: edges disintegrate on turningCosmetic — still crisps
## Adjustment Notes Salt only out of the oven — earlier salt draws moisture, softens crust. Undercrisp at service → a few more minutes, but this competes with the beef blast; accept as-is if the beef needs the oven. ## Scaling Notes Do not crowd — potatoes need space. Above 700 g, use two trays or the crust fails across the batch.

dishes.source: Recovered from rib-eye-roast-sunday.docx, generated for service Sun 12 Jul 2026 (no generation date stated in doc)
dishes.summary: Carrot batons steamed under a lid with butter, 1 tsp honey and a splash of water, then reduced uncovered to a light glossy glaze; optional lemon squeeze corrects any cloying sweetness.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview Carrots glazed in butter with a restrained touch of honey to a tender-yielding bite and light gloss — the warm sweet-soft counterpoint to the beef, honey held to 1 tsp so it doesn't stack richness against the wine. ## Yield & Timing *Yield: serves 3 · Total ~20 min · Active ~15 min · Induction* ## Flavor Architecture
ElementDefinition
BaseButter
Primary driverCarrot sweetness, lightly lifted by honey
AcidOptional lemon squeeze at finish — corrective, pulls back sweetness if cloying
Aromatic/finishSalt; optional pepper
*Acid single-stage at finish justified: glaze reduction; acid's role is corrective, not structural.* ## Texture Meal-level texture exemption — glazed carrots are inherently soft; contrast provided by crisp potatoes and beef crust across the plate. ## Prep Phase 1. Peel (skin turns leathery and bitter under a glaze). Even ~5 cm batons. ## Active Cooking 1. Carrots, butter, 1 tsp honey, ~50 ml water, pinch salt in a pan on induction 1. Cover, medium, ~8 min until a knife meets slight resistance. 2. Uncover, raise heat, reduce to a glossy glaze, ~4–5 min. Toss to coat. 3. Taste — if even slightly cloying, small squeeze of lemon. ## Holding & Assembly Cover, hold on residual heat up to 15 min. Glaze tightens — loosen with a splash of water off-heat before plating. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & CueRecovery
MajorGlaze breaks/scorches — reduced too hard. Cue: fat separates, brown flecks, acrid smellUnrecoverable if scorched. Prevention: reduce over medium, pull when glossy not sticky
MinorUndercooked core. Cue: knife meets hard resistanceSplash water, cover, 2–3 min more
## Adjustment Notes Too sweet → lemon squeeze. Flat → pinch of salt sharpens. Don't add honey at the end — won't integrate off-heat. ## Scaling Notes Not applicable.

dishes.name: Green Beans, Butter + Lemon Zest
dishes.source: Recovered from rib-eye-roast-sunday.docx, generated for service Sun 12 Jul 2026 (no generation date stated in doc)
dishes.summary: Trimmed green beans blanched 4 min in well-salted water, ice-shocked, held dry, then warmed through in butter at service with lemon zest added off-heat.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview Blanched green beans, shocked to hold color and bite, finished with butter and lemon zest for aromatic lift. The palate-resetting fresh-firm element against the rich plate. ## Yield & Timing *Yield: serves 3 · Total ~12 min · Active ~8 min · Induction* ## Flavor Architecture
ElementDefinition
BaseButter (finishing fat)
Primary driverGreen bean; vegetal-fresh
AcidNone — lemon zest is aromatic, not acid
Aromatic/finishLemon zest (volatile citrus + slight bitterness); optional garlic
*No-acid by design: fresh-finish component; brightness is aromatic (zest), not acidic. Meal acid lives in horseradish and jus.* ## Texture Two distinct — firm snap vs. tender core, held by blanch-and-shock. The plate's firmest element by design. ## Prep Phase 1. Trim beans. Zest the shared lemon (all zest → here); juice the lemon, reserve for adjustments. ## Active Cooking 1. Blanch in well-salted boiling water ~4 min — bright green, just tender with snap. 2. Ice-shock immediately — locks color and bite. Drain, dry well. 3. At 6:57: melt butter over low induction, toss beans to warm through ~2 min, add zest off-heat, salt to taste. ## Holding & Assembly Hold drained and dry, room temp, up to 15 min. Beans go into the butter cold and warm through — holding doesn't degrade them. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & CueRecovery
MajorOvercooked — blanched too long or not shocked. Cue: olive-drab, limp, no snapUnrecoverable. Prevention: 4 min max, immediate shock
MinorZest added on heat → bitter. Cue: acrid edgePrevention: zest off-heat only, at the very end
## Adjustment Notes Zest is the default for brightness without added sharpness; a few drops of lemon juice off-heat are a valid post-cook correction if it needs lift. Finishing salt at the toss if under-seasoned. ## Scaling Notes Not applicable.

dishes.summary: No-cook condiment of prepared horseradish folded into crème fraîche, tasted before any lemon or salt, held cold in the fridge for days and served straight from the fridge against the hot beef.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview Cold, sharp horseradish folded into crème fraîche — the acid-and-heat cutting agent for the rich beef. No-cook, make-ahead. ## Yield & Timing *Yield: ~100 ml · Total 5 min · Active 5 min · No heat* ## Flavor Architecture
ElementDefinition
BaseCrème fraîche
Primary driverHorseradish heat + pungency
AcidCrème fraîche tang + vinegar inherent to prepared horseradish; optional lemon
Aromatic/finish—
*Single-stage acid justified: no-cook condiment, acid inherent to the cultured cream and prepared horseradish.* ## Texture Meal-level exemption — a smooth condiment; contrast provided across the plate. Its job is flavor (sharp/cold), not texture. ## Prep Phase 1. Fold horseradish into crème fraîche. Taste before adding anything — prepared horseradish already carries vinegar and salt. Then adjust: pinch of salt if flat, lemon if it needs lift, more horseradish for bite. ## Active Cooking None. ## Holding & Assembly Fridge, covered, up to several days. Serve cold, straight from the fridge — the cold contrast against hot beef is part of its function. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & CueRecovery
MinorToo hot or too flat. Cue: overwhelms, or reads as plain creamFully adjustable: more crème fraîche to soften, more horseradish to sharpen
## Adjustment Notes Entirely tunable before service — soften with crème fraîche, sharpen with horseradish, brighten with lemon. Taste before salting. ## Scaling Notes Not applicable.

dishes.name: Red Wine Jus (Staged, Independent Reduction)
dishes.source: Recovered from rib-eye-roast-sunday.docx, generated for service Sun 12 Jul 2026 (no generation date stated in doc)
dishes.summary: Shallot-based red wine and beef stock reduction built independently of pan fond in three staged steps with an off-heat hold, enriched with roast drippings as available, reduced to ~150 ml light nappe and mounted with cold butter.
dishes.method_md:
## Dish Overview A concentrated red-wine-and-stock reduction built on browned shallot — not dependent on roast-pan fond, which a 250°F roast won't reliably produce. Staged with a hold to preserve the make-ahead without over-concentrating. Low-roast and post-blast drippings fold in as available. Reduced to a light nappe, mounted with cold butter. ## Yield & Timing *Yield: ~150 ml · Total ~45 min across stages · Active ~15 min · Outdoor gas* ## Flavor Architecture
ElementDefinition
BaseBrowned shallot fond (+ optional trimmings), built independently in the saucepan
Primary driverReduced beef stock + wine depth
AcidRed wine — staged early, reduced; acidity mellows and integrates
Aromatic/finishCold butter mount for gloss + body
*Acid staged correctly: wine in early, reduced to depth not sharpness.* ## Texture Meal-level exemption — a sauce; target is a light-syrup nappe coating a spoon back. ## Prep Phase 1. Finely slice 1 shallot. If using trimmings, have them ready. ## Active Cooking (staged) 1. Stage 1 (~4:45pm): brown shallot (+ optional trimmings) in a little oil over medium until deeply colored. Deglaze with wine, scraping the pan; reduce by half, ~5 min. Add stock, bring to a brief simmer, then off heat, covered. 2. Stage 2 (~6:05pm): return to gas, finish reducing to ~150 ml, lightly syrupy. Fold in low-roast drippings once the beef pulls. 3. Stage 3 (~6:40–6:43pm): off-heat, whisk in cold butter for gloss. Strain. Taste — salt sparingly (stock + drippings already salty). Hold warm on lowest gas. 4. After the beef's blast, pour any last drippings into the finished sauce and re-warm briefly. ## Holding & Assembly Warm on lowest gas up to 30 min. If sticky, loosen with a splash of stock and re-strain. ## Critical Control Points
SeverityFailure Mode & CueRecovery
MajorOver-reduced sticky/salty — reduced too far, or not held between stages. Cue: coats too thick, concentrated-saltyLoosen with stock/water; don't add salt. Prevention: stage with the off-heat hold; taste before final reduction
MinorButter mount breaks — added on too-high heat. Cue: oily, splitOff-heat, whisk in a splash of cold stock to re-emulsify
## Adjustment Notes If flat, a few drops of reserved lemon juice or a splash of wine lifts it. Salt last and sparingly — reduction concentrates existing salt. ## Scaling Notes Not applicable.
